note: Giving your opinion: a safe way to start in any conversation.
Agreeing: more natural than a bare “oui”. In everyday speech you will also hear “D'accord !” or “OK”.
A friendly greeting with friends and colleagues. Answer: Ça va bien, merci. Et toi ? More polite, with vous: Comment allez-vous ?
Everyday question with tu. Answer: Je viens du Maroc / de Syrie / d'Italie. With vous: Vous venez d'où ?

front: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie ?
note: Asking about someone's job. Answer without un or une: Je suis infirmière.

translations.pt: O que você faz da vida?

note: Answer: Je parle arabe, anglais et un peu français. Languages take no article after parler.
Answer: J'habite à Lyon / dans le quartier de la gare. With vous: Vous habitez où ?
Good: great company, and it gets you outside. Bad: it needs a walk every day.
Good: it doesn't need much space. Bad: it can scratch the furniture.
A small pet: it needs little space and little food. The h is aspiré: le hamster, never l'hamster.
You need to clean it every week.
Take your pet to the vet when it is ill: Je vais chez le vétérinaire (in speech: chez le véto).
Talk together: where to stay, what to do and how much it costs.
Planning a trip and making suggestions. On means “we” in everyday French.
Asking about money when you plan something together.

translations.en: How much do we want to spend?
